laws.rule: Brunei’s Sharia (Syariah) Penal Code came fully into effect in April 2019. Sharia law applies to: non-Muslims whether resident Bruneians or foreigners. It applies even when transiting on Brunei-registered aircraft and vessels. Non-Muslims may be arrested for being in close proximity with a Muslim of the opposite sex under the Sharia Penal Code - an offence known as khalwat. Common law and courts operate in parallel with the Sharia Penal Code and courts. Serious crimes can attract: the death penalty physical punishment imprisonment Crimes that attract the death penalty include: drugs (consumption, possession, selling/trafficking) blasphemy sodomy adultery rape murder
laws.heading: Sharia law

laws.rule: Some drug offences carry a mandatory death penalty. Other penalties include long prison sentences and physical punishment.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is observed. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, eating, drinking and smoking in public, between sunrise and sunset may be illegal. Even if you're not observing Ramadan, avoid these activities around people who are. Seek local advice to avoid offence. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: To drive in Brunei for up to 1 year, you need both: an Australian driver's licence (a digital driver's licence may not be accepted) a valid international driving permit (IDP) Driving without an IDP could void your travel and vehicle insurance.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Alcohol can be brought in only by non-Muslims aged 17 or over, for personal use and for drinking at a private residence: 2 bottles of liquor (1 litre each) or up to 12 cans of beer (330 mL each) per person. You must declare it to a Customs officer, and a later import must be at least 48 hours after the last one. Alcoholic liquors are on the restricted imports list of the Customs import order.
laws.penalty_signal: A false or incorrect declaration is an offence under section 138 of the Customs Order 2006.

laws.rule: There is no personal concession for bringing cigarettes into Brunei; they pay excise duty of BND 0.50 a stick. Cigarettes without a health warning on the pack are a prohibited import. Tobacco products and vaporisers (vapes), including e-liquid, are listed as restricted imports, which means they need permission and are not a free personal allowance.
laws.penalty_signal: A false or incorrect declaration is an offence under section 138 of the Customs Order 2006.

laws.rule: The Customs import order lists opium and chandu as prohibited imports, and 'poisons and deleterious drugs' as restricted imports. The list does not set out which medicines count; ask the Royal Customs and Excise Department before bringing prescription medicines.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress and behaviour standards are conservative. Take care not to offend. If in doubt, seek local advice. Be cautious when making comments about local issues, particularly those relating to the royal family. You could cause offence or even attract legal consequences. On Fridays, businesses, including shops and restaurants, close from 12pm to 2pm for prayers. Government offices and local schools do not operate on Friday. They open on Saturday instead. Brunei Tourism: dress modestly in public. At mosques, women cover head, shoulders and knees, and everyone removes their shoes. Don't walk in front of people praying or touch the Qur'an. Ask before photographing people, mosques or government buildings. Businesses close on Fridays from 12 to 2 pm. During Ramadan, don't eat, drink or smoke in public in daylight.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: A visa is needed; Brunei's foreign ministry lists Australia for a 30-day visa on arrival. Before arrival, complete the online e-Arrival Card and the BruHealth health declaration, and hold medical insurance: without proof of insurance the visa is limited to 2 weeks.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: 30-day visa on arrival at any Brunei immigration post.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Complete the e-Arrival Card (up to 3 days before arrival) and the BruHealth Health Declaration Form, buy medical insurance (tourists at least BND 10,000 cover), and carry a valid air ticket.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: 30 days on a visa on arrival; check the entry stamp for the length given. Overstaying can bring imprisonment and caning.

steps.step: Complete the e-Arrival Card online before arriving (and before departing), by air, land or sea.
Complete the Health Declaration Form on BruHealth before arrival.
Buy medical insurance for the whole stay (tourists: at least BND 10,000) and carry proof for the immigration post.
Get the visa on arrival at the immigration post and check the entry stamp for the stay given.
Crossing by land or sea: apply online through the Exit and Entry System (EES) first.

documents: Passport valid at least 6 months on entry
Medical insurance proof (BND 10,000 minimum for tourists)
